title: Utility API
description: Generate and customize utility families with the Tremplin Sass API.
lead: Configure utility families with Sass maps, canonical prefixes and explicit composition properties.

sections.heading: API explained
paragraphs: Tremplin generates utility families from its configurable Sass map. Configure the utilities map before loading an entry. Custom family definitions replace existing definitions shallowly; they do not merge every nested option automatically.

Both the full entry and the focused utilities entry accept the utilities map. The focused entry includes root tokens, helpers and mapped utilities, not Reboot or components. Configure the shared config module first when changing breakpoint or spacing maps. This guide describes the pinned source, including limitations rather than compatibility aliases.

paragraphs: Missing required keys, invalid selector modes and malformed boolean flags produce Sass errors when the family is generated. Unknown keys warn. State identifiers and attribute patterns are not fully validated: use trusted build-time configuration and inspect generated CSS. A disabled family is omitted before those generator checks.

sections.heading: Canonical variant names
sections.example: Stacked below mdInline from md

code.source: Stacked below mdInline from md

paragraphs: Write colons literally in HTML; CSS selectors escape them. md:d-flex uses the 768px viewport minimum. The canonical default tiers are xs, sm, md, lg, xl and 2xl. Infix forms and xxl aliases are not generated.

Variants exist only when the family enables them. Display is responsive by default but has no default print variants. Opacity does not have automatic hover/focus variants. A custom family with state: hover focus-visible can generate hover:project-fade-50 and md:focus-visible:project-fade-50. Use an empty list to omit states; true and false generate literal unusable pseudo-class names rather than expanding to hover/focus.

Base and viewport rules are emitted first, print follows, and OS-dark rules come last. dark: uses prefers-color-scheme, independently of data-trm-theme. These are viewport/media variants, not container queries.

sections.heading: Property and value formats
paragraphs: A property list receives the same value on every property. A property map supplies defaults overridden by per-value property maps. A scalar value or null value key has no suffix; an explicit null class uses the value key as the class name.

A named null value does not universally remove a class: property-map defaults are still emitted at this pin. Scalar-property nulls omit their declaration. Remove a whole family with null or replace its values map deliberately rather than assuming a null value erases every generated rule.

sections.heading: Composition properties

code.source: Composed color

paragraphs: Explicit custom property names in property are preserved exactly. Assigned custom properties are registered globally once with syntax: "*" and inherits: false; referenced root/theme tokens are not registered merely because they appear in a value. Normal color still inherits into descendants even when the private composition property does not.
Use explicit property maps when matching emitted names to non-inheriting registrations matters. This pattern avoids the separate variables helper namespace mismatch.

sections.heading: Variables helper limitation
paragraphs: The variables helper always prefixes emitted names with --trm-, while its registration pass prepends only -- to the supplied key. These names disagree at this pin. Actual helper-emitted variables can therefore inherit; do not assume the registration isolates them. Pre-prefixed or empty keys are not normalized or rejected consistently.

A variables map emits static values; a scalar/list receives the current utility value. This guide records that behavior rather than silently patching the clone. Prefer the explicit property-map example above for predictable composition and keep variable names non-empty trusted literals.

sections.heading: Attribute selectors
paragraphs: attr-starts matches the start of the entire class attribute. A different class written first prevents a match. attr-includes matches a substring anywhere, including within another class name; neither is a whitespace-separated class-token selector. Value suffixes and responsive/print/dark prefixes do not change the attribute pattern itself.

A class key is required, but empty/null patterns and attribute-state combinations are not rejected semantically. Attribute states produce an unrelated empty-name class selector, not a useful state-qualified attribute rule. Use class selector mode for states.

Patterns are interpolated into CSS without automatic double-quote escaping. A literal double quote can cause a Sass selector parse error; backslashes require deliberate Sass/CSS escaping. Avoid complex or untrusted patterns instead of relying on validation the pin does not provide.

sections.heading: Child selectors
paragraphs: The entire selector is wrapped in :where(), including compound prefixes and pseudo-classes, for zero selector specificity. This targets the requested children rather than the parent. Normal cascade layers, importance and source order still apply. Do not assume HTML class order chooses a winner.

sections.heading: Add utilities

code.source: Explicit print and dark variants

paragraphs: Custom definitions join the default map. Supply explicit state names and opt into print/dark as needed. CSS opacity affects the entire element, including text and focus indicators; check contrast and do not use opacity to communicate status by itself.

sections.heading: Override and remove utilities
paragraphs: A family replacement is shallow: include property, values and every desired flag. This example removes floats, replaces opacity values and states, and omits the disabled cursor family. Null, false and disabled definitions do not emit registration or variant output.

sections.heading: Importance
paragraphs: Utility property declarations have normal priority by default. important: true applies to property declarations in the selected family in every generated mode. Declarations emitted through the separate variables helper remain normal; explicit property-map assignments obey the property importance flag. There is no global enable-important-utilities switch. Helper/Reboot declarations have their own contracts, so this option is not a framework-wide removal of importance.

sections.heading: Motion and preferences

code.source: Optional decorative motion

paragraphs: The pinned automatic reduced-motion guard names only the flat animation-shake and animation-pop classes. It does not automatically cancel renamed custom classes or higher-specificity state variants. Add an explicit application preference rule to each animated element, as shown, rather than claiming those variants are universally protected.

This example uses normal utility importance. If you opt into important animation declarations, review layer order and selector specificity again. Turning enable-reduced-motion off opts out of the built-in guard; it is not an accessibility improvement.

sections.heading: Verify your build
paragraphs: Compile the documented maps, inspect selectors and registrations, and test computed styles at real boundaries. Check screen/print, OS-dark versus explicit theme, keyboard states, reduced motion, RTL and narrow content. The examples describe the fixed source revision; they do not certify every possible custom map.
Related utility-family guides are being migrated separately. Do not infer aliases, variants or old APIs from a guide that has not yet been updated.

code.source:
# Framework repository
npm.cmd run test:sass:utility-api
npm.cmd run build:css
npm.cmd run check:size

sections.heading: Configuration and limits
paragraphs: Do not infer responsive, dark, print or state variants from a base selector. Family definitions and helper layers have separate contracts. The default declarations have normal priority; inspect configuration and generated CSS before adding flags.

sections.heading: Opacity and inheritance
paragraphs: fg-* assigns the non-inheriting --trm-fg composition token. fg-50 mixes that local role with transparent; there is no currentcolor fallback, so pair it with a role. Ordinary CSS color still inherits. fg-reset explicitly inherits the composition token; it is not a hard-coded body color. Lower alpha and weaker role levels can fail text contrast.

sections.heading: Configure foreground roles
paragraphs: Configure the owning theme module before the entry. Theme maps merge shallowly at their top level: replacing one color replaces its whole role map. Use null to remove an exact map key; numeric and quoted string keys are distinct. Test actual pairs in light/dark and forced colors; the pin adds no special CanvasText reminting.

sections.heading: Verification
paragraphs: Test actual content at narrow widths, in both directions, after changing theme/OS preference, and with zoom and supported assistive technology. Role names, reduced alpha and decorative effects are not accessibility guarantees.
Continue to Utility API for configuration and pinned limitations. Compiled selectors prove availability, not universal browser feature support.

sections.heading: Responsive gaps
paragraphs: md:row-gap-4 applies at the default md minimum viewport width of 768px. Only prefix-style responsive names are generated. Each gap family is responsive by default; print, dark, and state variants require a family override. With equal importance and specificity, the generated cascade order decides the result, not class order in the HTML. Base axis controls follow base gap shorthands, but a wider responsive shorthand can replace both axes; override that axis at the same breakpoint when needed.

sections.heading: Gap configuration
paragraphs: The gap family now uses the same configurable utility map as row-gap and column-gap. Remove a family with null, disable it with enabled: false, or replace its definition. No handwritten gap-* rules are left behind. Definitions are replaced shallowly: supply property, class, values, and any desired flags. The shared spacer map also affects other spacing and gutter helpers. Utilities are not important by default; opt in with important: true on a family, not a global flag.

sections.heading: Track counts and full-width items
paragraphs: grid-cols-1, grid-cols-2, grid-cols-3, grid-cols-4, and grid-cols-6 create equal 1fr tracks, matching the upstream values. There is no default grid-cols-5. Unlike minmax(0, 1fr), a plain 1fr track retains its automatic minimum: long intrinsic content can overflow a narrow box. Use min-w-0, wrapping, and suitable content sizing where needed.

grid-cols-fill belongs on a grid item and sets grid-column: 1 / -1 across all explicit columns. It is not a column count. Use md:grid-cols-3 for the canonical responsive prefix. Grid utilities use shared viewport breakpoints, not container-query variants; infix aliases are not generated.

sections.heading: Subgrid
paragraphs: Place d-grid grid-cols-subgrid on a grid item that spans multiple parent columns to reuse their track lines and column spacing. Add grid-cols-fill to span the entire explicit parent grid. Subgrid is only useful inside a parent Grid; it does not create a standalone set of equal tracks. Check your supported browser versions before depending on it.

sections.heading: Auto-placement and reading order
paragraphs: grid-auto-flow-row places items by row; grid-auto-flow-column places them by column. Set rows and implicit column sizing as appropriate for column flow. grid-auto-flow-dense enables dense row packing, which can visually move later items into earlier holes. CSS placement does not reorder the DOM, reading order, or keyboard tab order. Avoid dense placement for ordered, interactive content when the visual order would become misleading.

sections.heading: Utilities versus layout helpers
paragraphs: Use d-grid for this utility-first API. The grid layout container defaults to twelve 1fr tracks, a 1.5rem gap and inline-size containment. Ordinary children auto-place normally; g-col/g-start set literal placement. Keep track counts and item spans coherent to avoid implicit tracks. See the CSS Grid guide for container-responsive placement.

The new utility families remain available when $enable-cssgrid is false; that switch controls only the layout helper module. Utility removal and configuration use the grid-column-counts, grid-columns, and grid-auto-flow map keys. Declarations are not important by default. Set important: true on an individual mapped family when needed; there is no global importance flag.

code.source: @use 'tremplin/scss/tremplin-utilities' with ($utilities: ('animation': null));
